name: One surface, and a way to search it
summary: The release cut from living with 1.6.2 for a while. Everything in it came from using the application rather than from a plan, and the two largest items turned out to be the same defect seen from different sides: the product had more than one renderer, and they disagreed. Split's formatted pane and the print/PDF surface shared a 43-line renderer built from regular expressions over lines; enumerated against sixteen ordinary markdown constructs, sixteen were wrong. Print is the half that mattered most, because a PDF leaves the application and cannot be corrected once sent. Print now goes through a real parser, and Split simply shows the editor itself, so the two surfaces cannot drift apart again because there is only one of them. Adopting a real parser removed an accident that had been doing security work: the old renderer emitted text nodes, so hostile markup in an opened document never became an element. That guarantee is now stated deliberately by a sanitizer rather than inherited from an implementation detail. The release also carries the first document search this product has had, the ribbon and mode controls the feedback asked for, and the naming and repository work prepared for 1.6.3, which was recorded complete but never tagged or published.

required.title: Print and PDF export render through a real parser
required.summary: The split preview and print/PDF export shared a 43-line renderer that matched constructs with regular expressions over lines. Enumerated against sixteen ordinary constructs, SIXTEEN were wrong: a GFM table became paragraphs of pipe characters, an ordered list lost its numbering and became bullets, nested lists flattened, task lists kept literal brackets, emphasis inside a heading or blockquote stayed as asterisks, and a hard-wrapped paragraph split in two. The editor was correct throughout, so the two disagreed about one document. Both now render through vendored markdown-it with the footnote and task-list plugins, which is what makes the dialect CommonMark plus GFM rather than CommonMark alone. Sixteen of sixteen verified correct, pinned by construct rather than by markup so a future renderer that regresses one differently still fails. (#134)

required.title: Rendered document HTML passes an allowlist sanitizer
required.summary: Rendering with html:true preserves the inline HTML this dialect round-trips, and hands every byte of an opened document into a DOM that shares an origin with the native bindings, where a javascript: URL reaches SaveDocument and OpenRecentDocument with no path restriction. The renderer this replaced was safe from that ONLY BY ACCIDENT: it emitted text nodes, so hostile markup never became an element. sanitize.js states the guarantee deliberately — element, attribute and URL-scheme allowlists, never denylists. markdown-it's own validateLink is disabled so the sanitizer is the single URL authority; that is not a relaxation, but it moves the refusal somewhere it can be SEEN, since a link refused during parsing leaves no element and went unrecorded. Refusals now surface as link.refused and image.refused, deduped per distinct value and capped so a document already judged hostile cannot evict the rest of the trail. (#134)

required.title: Split shows the real editor, not a second rendering
required.summary: Split's formatted pane was a preview drawn by the separate renderer. It carried its own typography scale — h1 at 32px against the editor's 36px, its own blockquote and pre styling — and it was READ-ONLY, so the formatted half of split was the one surface in a WYSIWYG editor you could not type into. Fixing the renderer only narrows that gap, so the editor element now moves into the pane instead. The instance is not rebuilt to move it: reparenting a live ProseMirror tree preserves content, editability and serialization, measured before the design was built on it. Both panes are live editors over one document, so an explicit authority — the pane the user last pressed a key or pointer in — decides which one wins. (#134)

required.title: The document can be searched, and text replaced
required.summary: The application had no document search; the only search in it filtered the file list. The obstacle was never the text box: the document is shown in three substrates, and a search over whichever surface was visible would answer differently in each — in Split, differently from itself. A match is therefore an offset range into the markdown SOURCE, the one coordinate every mode shares, and each surface reveals a source range in its own terms. Replace rewrites the source and remounts, the same shape as every other document command, which is the answer to the re-serialization hazard: an edit driven through the editor would rewrite lines the user never touched. Find, Find and Replace, Find Next and Find Previous are on the Edit menu, because a menu item's key equivalent is matched before web content sees the event. (#132)

required.title: Embedded images no longer distort when switching to Split
required.summary: The image node view measured its container with getBoundingClientRect, which reports ZOOMED pixels, and wrote an explicit height from it; the width then derived from that height. At a document zoom of 0.9 a 538px pane measured 484, and every switch compounded it. clientWidth is the layout width and is unaffected by zoom. Fixed as a vendor patch, since the measurement is inside the vendored bundle. (#131)

required.title: Formatted, Raw and Split are one control
required.summary: Mode selection was two separate controls for what is one choice between three states. It is now a single radiogroup, which is also what makes the current mode announceable rather than inferred from which of two buttons looks pressed. (#129)

required.title: File is a menu, not a ribbon tab
required.summary: File was a ribbon tab, so opening it replaced the ribbon's contents and took the formatting controls away to show a list of file commands. It is now a dropdown that leaves the ribbon alone, and the ribbon opens on Format. (#130)

required.title: The ribbon reads as a toolbar, not a row of pills
required.summary: Ribbon commands were bordered, filled, rounded buttons — the look of a web page rather than a desktop toolbar. They are now borderless and transparent at rest and show their affordance on hover and press, while controls that genuinely are fields keep their borders. (#133)

required.title: The naming and repository work prepared for 1.6.3
required.summary: Recorded complete under 1.6.3 and never tagged or published, so it reaches users here. The application is named Dr Markdown everywhere: macOS strips a .app suffix for display only when the basename has no other dot, so the period in 'Dr.' was the whole reason the launcher showed the extension. Build artifacts no longer appear in the launcher, ephemeral documentation is out of the repository, and the build can produce a notarized DMG under DRMD_SIGN_IDENTITY and DRMD_NOTARY_PROFILE.

deferred.title: Exact in-place match selection in the formatted surface
deferred.summary: DEFERRED because it requires source-offset to editor-position mapping, which is a separate piece of work held on the unmerged probe/source-range-patching branch — the same machinery the standing re-serialization blocker needs. Shipping search without it costs precision in ONE surface and nothing else: the match count is identical in all three modes because it is computed from the source, Raw and Split's source pane select the matched characters exactly, and the formatted surface scrolls to and marks the block the match falls in. Doing the mapping first would have delayed a feature the product had none of.

deferred.title: Raw inline <svg> in a document is not rendered
deferred.summary: DEFERRED, and it is a real fidelity loss taken knowingly. An inline <svg> carries its own script elements and its own xlink: URL surface — a second sanitizer's worth of rules — so it is dropped rather than partially trusted. Mermaid diagrams are unaffected: they are injected after the sanitizing pass. Revisit only with a reason to accept that surface, not to close a gap for its own sake.

workstreams.name: One document, one rendering of it
workstreams.summary: The product had more than one renderer and they disagreed. This is the work that reduced it to one.

workstreams.summary: 1.6.3 was recorded complete and never tagged or published. Its work is real and reaches users here.

blockers.title: The WYSIWYG surface still re-serializes the whole document
blockers.summary: Carried forward unchanged, and now with one more thing depending on it. An edit through the editor re-serializes the document, so lines the user never touched can be rewritten. Search sidesteps it by replacing through the SOURCE, but the same gap is why a match cannot be selected exactly in the formatted surface. Only source-preserving editing closes the class; the unmerged probe/source-range-patching branch holds a spike at it.
